newsitem.title: DUBAI: SABIC to open MTBE plant this month.
newsitem.headline: SABIC to open MTBE plant this month.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's industrial giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) will this month officially inaugurate its 700,000-tonne-a-year MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether) plant, the Saudi industry and electricity minister was on Sunday quoted as saying.
The Saudi English-language Arab News daily quoted Hashem bin Abdullah bin Hashem Yamani as saying the plant in the industrial city of Jubail will be opened in the second week of this month.
The plant, operated by SABIC subsidiary Saudi Petrochemical Co (SADAF), will raise the kingdom's MTBE annual capacity to 2.6 million tonnes. MTBE is an additive which makes gasoline burn cleanly.
SADAF is a 50-50 joint venture between SABIC and Pecten Arabia Co, a unit of Shell Oil Co of the U.S., itself an affiliate of Royal/Dutch Shell Group.
SABIC officials had said initial commissioning of the plant, which will also produce ethyl tertiary butyl ether (ETBE), began last summer.
SABIC, which accounts for five percent of total world production of petrochemicals, currently has three MTBE plants producing 1.9 million tonnes a year.

Arab News quoted Yamani as saying SABIC's total production capacity will reach more than 28 million tonnes by the year 2000. SABIC's 17 plants produce 22 million tonnes of various petrochemical products, the paper said.
